subject: Business
title: Lean Manufacturing: Eliminating Waste
description: A micro-lesson that makes Lean Manufacturing: Eliminating Waste usable.

hook.text: Toyota produces more cars with fewer defects using less space than any other automaker.

buildup.text: Lean identifies seven wastes: overproduction, waiting, transport, overprocessing, inventory, motion, and defects.

discovery.text: Any activity that doesn't add value from the customer's perspective is waste — and a target for elimination.

twist.text: Lean isn't about cutting staff. It's about making processes so efficient that the same people produce more value.

climax.text: Virginia Mason Medical Center applied lean principles from Toyota. Patient wait times dropped 50%.

punchline.text: Do more with less. But start by removing what adds nothing.

quiz.question: How many types of waste does lean manufacturing identify?

details.summary: Lean manufacturing is a production philosophy that systematically eliminates waste across seven categories: overproduction, waiting, transport, overprocessing, inventory, motion, and defects. Originating from Toyota, lean principles optimize every step to deliver maximum customer value.
details.whyItMatters: Lean manufacturing transformed global industry by proving that eliminating waste improves both quality and cost simultaneously. Its principles extend beyond factories into services, healthcare, and software development as lean thinking.
takeaways: Seven wastes provide a framework for identifying inefficiency in any process
Continuous improvement and respect for people are lean's core pillars
Value stream mapping visualizes waste across the entire production flow

faq.question: What are the seven wastes of lean manufacturing?
faq.answer: Overproduction (making more than needed), waiting (idle time), transport (unnecessary movement of goods), overprocessing (doing more than required), inventory (excess stock), motion (unnecessary human movement), and defects (rework and scrap). Some add an eighth: unused talent.

faq.question: How does value stream mapping work?
faq.answer: Teams map every step from raw material to customer delivery, recording cycle times, wait times, inventory levels, and information flows. The current-state map reveals waste. A future-state map designs the improved flow, guiding specific improvement projects.
